isolation.evidence: Fresh general-purpose subagent (Agent tool, model alias fable) dispatched with only the frozen prompt.md text plus an opaque scratch output path outside the repository. No coordinator conversation, sibling outputs, or evaluation criteria were passed in. The worker report describes only its own file and tests; it does not mention reading any sibling take.

limitations: Worker was a Claude Code subagent inside the coordinator's session. User-level Claude Code configuration (global CLAUDE.md, output style, enabled MCP servers) applied to the worker context.
Output path was an opaque scratch folder outside the repository, so no sibling take sat beside the worker's write location; the repository tree remained reachable on the shared host filesystem.
Nine cells for this model ran concurrently and shared the coordinator's in-app browser pane, so a sibling take's rendered page could be visible to a worker that tested in the browser.
Reasoning effort 'xhigh' comes from harness settings (effortLevel: xhigh in ~/.claude/settings.json, inherited by subagents), not from a runtime response field.
Model requested through the Agent tool alias 'fable'; in this Claude Code session that alias is Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1). The runtime did not report the worker's effective model ID.
durationMs is the harness-reported subagent duration; completedAt is startedAt plus that duration. startedAt is the coordinator's launch clock for the wave.

Worker reported that the shared browser pane was hidden for most of its session, so requestAnimationFrame was throttled there; it verified continuous playback by stepping its own frame function in code rather than by watching live playback.

Worker reported running pkill -f "headless=new" to stop its own stuck headless Chrome and noted this may also have terminated headless Chrome processes belonging to sibling cells running on the same machine.
Output loads external resources at runtime: https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js
